facts.text: The Black Belt Teacher Corps Teach for Alabama scholarship is available to junior, senior, or Alt. A education students in initial certification programs, offering up to $10,000 in savings with service teaching in Alabama public schools in the Black Belt region, rural schools, or high-needs schools.

sources.title: BBTC Scholarship | UWA Online
sources.quote: This scholarship is available to any University of West Alabama junior/senior and Alt. A education student (on-campus or online) in a program providing initial certification who meets the other criteria listed on the application.

sources.title: BBTC Scholarship | UWA Online
sources.quote: Each semester the scholarship is active, the award is $2,500 (up to a maximum of $10,000).

sources.title: BBTC Scholarship | UWA Online
sources.quote: Based on the scholarship awarded, students will complete service teaching in Alabama public schools in the Black Belt region, designated rural schools or in high-needs schools.

facts.text: The school was chartered in 1835 as a female academy and in 1883 established normal school training under Julia Tutwiler, which university archives believe was the first State appropriation in Alabama made exclusively for the education of women.

sources.title: History | UWA Online
sources.quote: The University of West Alabama was chartered in 1835 as a church-related female academy and admitted its first students in 1839.

sources.title: History | UWA Online
sources.quote: Julia Tutwiler, who succeeded in getting a small appropriation from the State Legislature in 1883 to establish normal school training for girls at Livingston Female Academy.

sources.title: History | UWA Online
sources.quote: According to statements in the University archives, this is believed to be the first State appropriation in Alabama made exclusively for the education of women.
